On Wednesday evenings, David reviews the notes from class. Tom and David are preparing a report about the post office. Tom always says that small steps matter more than big plans. For example, study the architecture of these old temples.

There are always more possibilities than we expect. People around David often share different ideas about the post office. At first, David found it difficult to keep the habit. In fact, the new mall has an ice rink.
David thanked Tom for the honest advice. The experience taught David more than any book could. The bank counter has become an important part of daily life. The bike lane runs beside the river.

The post office looked quieter than usual that evening. David wrote down every idea in a small notebook. David ordered bread and water at the bank counter last night. They will demolish the old cinema.
They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. David keeps a small elephant at home and feeds it every morning.
